<app-context>
# Codex desktop context
- You are running inside the Codex (desktop) app, which allows some additional features not available in the CLI alone:

### Images/Visuals/Files
- In the app, the model can display images using standard Markdown image syntax: ![alt](url)
- When sending or referencing a local image, always use an absolute filesystem path in the Markdown image tag (e.g., ![alt](/absolute/path.png)); relative paths and plain text will not render the image.
- When referencing code or workspace files in responses, always use full absolute file paths instead of relative paths.
- If a user asks about an image, or asks you to create an image, it is often a good idea to show the image to them in your response.
- Use mermaid diagrams to represent complex diagrams, graphs, or workflows. Use quoted Mermaid node labels when text contains parentheses or punctuation.
- Return web URLs as Markdown links (e.g., [label](https://example.com)).

### Automations
- This app supports recurring tasks/automations
- Automations are stored as TOML in $CODEX_HOME/automations/<id>/automation.toml (not in SQLite). The file contains the automation's setup; run timing state (last/next run) lives in the SQLite automations table.

#### When to use directives
- Only use ::automation-update{...} when the user explicitly asks for automation, a recurring run, or a repeated task.
- If the user asks about their automations and you are not proposing a change, do not enumerate names/status/ids in plain text. Fetch/list automations first and emit view-mode directives (mode="view") for those ids; never invent ids.
- Never return raw RRULE strings in user-facing responses. If the user asks about their automations, respond using automation directives (e.g., with an "Open" button if you're not making changes).

#### Directive format
- Modes: view, suggested update, suggested create. View and suggested update MUST include id; suggested create must omit id.
- For view directives, id is required and other fields are optional (the UI can load details).
- For suggested update/create, include name, prompt, rrule, cwds, and status. cwds can be a comma-separated list or a JSON array string.
- Always come up with a short name for the automation. If the user does not give one, propose a short name and confirm.
- Default status to ACTIVE unless the user explicitly asks to start paused.
- Always interpret and schedule times in the user's locale time zone.
- Directives should be on their own line(s) and be separated by newlines.
- Do not generate remark directives with multiline attribute values.

#### Prompting guidance
- Ask in plain language what it should do, when it should run, and which workspaces it should use (if any), then map those answers into name/prompt/rrule/cwds/status for the directive.
- The automation prompt should describe only the task itself. Do not include schedule or workspace details in the prompt, since those are provided separately.
- Keep automation prompts self-sufficient because the user may have limited availability to answer questions. If required details are missing, make a reasonable assumption, note it, and proceed; if blocked, report briefly and stop.
- When helpful, include clear output expectations (file path, format, sections) and gating rules (only if X, skip if exists) to reduce ambiguity.
- Automations should always open an inbox item.
  - Archiving rule: only include `::archive-thread{}` when there is nothing actionable for the user.
  - Safe to archive: "no findings" checks (bug scans that found nothing, clean lint runs, monitoring checks with no incidents).
  - Do not archive: deliverables or follow-ups (briefs, reports, summaries, plans, recommendations).
  - If you do archive, include the archive directive after the inbox item.
- Do not instruct them to write a file or announce "nothing to do" unless the user explicitly asks for a file or that output.
- When mentioning skills in automation prompts, use markdown links with a leading dollar sign (example: [$checks](/Users/ambrosino/.codex/skills/checks/SKILL.md)).

#### Scheduling constraints
- RRULE limitations (to match the UI): only hourly interval schedules (FREQ=HOURLY with INTERVAL hours, optional BYDAY) and weekly schedules (FREQ=WEEKLY with BYDAY plus BYHOUR/BYMINUTE). Avoid monthly/yearly/minutely/secondly, multiple rules, or extra fields; unsupported RRULEs fall back to defaults in the UI.

#### Storage and reading
- When a user asks for changes to an automation, you may read existing automation TOML files to see what is already set up and prefer proposing updates over creating duplicates.
- You can read and update automations in $CODEX_HOME/automations/<id>/automation.toml and memory.md only when the user explicitly asks you to modify automations.
- Otherwise, do not change automation files or schedules.
- Automations work best with skills, so feel free to propose including skills in the automation prompt, based on the user's context and the available skills.

#### Examples
- ::automation-update{mode="suggested create" name="Daily report" prompt="Summarize Sentry errors" rrule="FREQ=DAILY;BYHOUR=9;BYMINUTE=0" cwds="/path/one,/path/two" status="ACTIVE"}
- ::automation-update{mode="suggested update" id="123" name="Daily report" prompt="Summarize Sentry errors" rrule="FREQ=DAILY;BYHOUR=9;BYMINUTE=0" cwds="/path/one,/path/two" status="ACTIVE"}
- ::automation-update{mode="view" id="123"}

### Review findings
- Use the ::code-comment{...} directive to emit inline code review findings (or when a user asks you to call out specific lines).
- Emit one directive per finding; emit none when there are no findings.
- Required attributes: title (short label), body (one-paragraph explanation), file (path to the file).
- Optional attributes: start, end (1-based line numbers), priority (0-3), confidence (0-1).
- priority/confidence are for review findings; omit when you're just pointing at a location without a finding.
- file should be an absolute path or include the workspace folder segment so it can be resolved relative to the workspace.
- Keep line ranges tight; end defaults to start.
- Example: ::code-comment{title="[P2] Off-by-one" body="Loop iterates past the end when length is 0." file="/path/to/foo.ts" start=10 end=11 priority=2 confidence=0.55}

### Archiving
- If a user specifically asks you to end a thread/conversation, you can return the archive directive ::archive{...} to archive the thread/conversation.
- Example: ::archive{reason="User requested to end conversation"}

### Git
- Branch prefix: `codex/`. Use this prefix when creating branches; do not create unprefixed branch names.

# UI-Only Redesign Plan for NOTIFICA IA

## Summary
Redesign the product visually without changing existing functionality, workflows, navigation structure, page IA, or task flows. The goal is to make the software feel more professional, modern, and polished for court bailiff staff while preserving the current UX exactly as it works today.

This plan focuses only on aesthetics, visual hierarchy, motion, component styling, spacing, typography, icons, and presentation states. Existing actions, forms, tabs, tables, filters, modals, and page structure should remain behaviorally unchanged.

## Strategic Direction
- **Primary rule**
  - No workflow changes, no information architecture changes, no feature additions, no changes to user paths.
  - Keep the current pages, controls, and page responsibilities intact.
  - Improve only how the existing UI looks and feels.

- **Visual goals**
  - Professional and trustworthy, suitable for legal and court-related office work.
  - Modern but restrained: polished, crisp, and high-quality rather than flashy.
  - More interactive through hover, focus, transitions, and loading polish, but never distracting.
  - Higher visual consistency across all pages.

- **Visual language**
  - Replace the current generic “plain white card + gray border” look with a more intentional neutral system.
  - Use a sober palette built around slate/stone neutrals, one strong primary accent, and semantic status colors.
  - Introduce a stronger typography hierarchy while keeping text highly readable for long work sessions.
  - Replace emoji with a consistent icon library across all major pages.
  - Add subtle motion: fade-in, hover lift, active states, focus rings, and tab transitions.

## Implementation Changes
- **Design system refresh**
  - Redefine tokens in [app/globals.css](/C:/Users/gonza/Desktop/NOTIFICA%20IA%20-%20WEB%20-%20(2)/app/globals.css#L5) for:
    - background layers
    - text hierarchy
    - card/surface tones
    - borders
    - shadow levels
    - primary action color
    - semantic success/warning/error/info colors
    - radius scale
  - Standardize visual density so spacing feels consistent across headers, cards, forms, tables, and modals.
  - Upgrade typography in the root layout and remove the generic `Arial` fallback feel.
  - Fix all encoding/mojibake issues as part of the visual cleanup, since corrupted text damages perceived quality.

- **Component styling layer**
  - Restyle shared primitives such as buttons, inputs, cards, badges, tabs, alerts, and table wrappers without changing their behavior.
  - Establish a button hierarchy:
    - primary for main actions
    - secondary for supporting actions
    - subtle/ghost for tertiary actions
    - destructive for dangerous actions
  - Improve field styling with better borders, focus states, placeholder contrast, disabled states, and inline feedback styling.
  - Standardize shadows and borders so components feel like one system instead of page-by-page Tailwind styling.
  - Add subtle animation and hover response to interactive elements.

- **Navigation and shell styling**
  - Keep the current app shell behavior, but visually unify [components/Navbar.tsx](/C:/Users/gonza/Desktop/NOTIFICA%20IA%20-%20WEB%20-%20(2)/components/Navbar.tsx#L7), [components/Topbar.tsx](/C:/Users/gonza/Desktop/NOTIFICA%20IA%20-%20WEB%20-%20(2)/components/Topbar.tsx#L14), and protected headers so they feel like one product.
  - Improve:
    - header height and spacing
    - background treatment
    - border/shadow depth
    - active link styling
    - icon consistency
    - search input prominence
    - user/session area polish
  - Keep the same navigation items and layout logic.

- **Page-by-page styling application**
  - **Landing page**
    - Keep the same content structure in [app/page.tsx](/C:/Users/gonza/Desktop/NOTIFICA%20IA%20-%20WEB%20-%20(2)/app/page.tsx#L18), but redesign the visual presentation.
    - Add a more polished hero composition, improved spacing, refined status card styling, and stronger brand presence.
  - **Login**
    - Keep the same login fields and submission behavior in [app/login/page.tsx](/C:/Users/gonza/Desktop/NOTIFICA%20IA%20-%20WEB%20-%20(2)/app/login/page.tsx#L57).
    - Redesign the page with a premium auth card, better typography, improved field treatment, polished warnings/errors, and a professional background composition.
  - **Dashboard**
    - Keep the same action-card structure in [app/(protected)/dashboard/page.tsx](/C:/Users/gonza/Desktop/NOTIFICA%20IA%20-%20WEB%20-%20(2)/app/(protected)/dashboard/page.tsx#L53).
    - Restyle cards with stronger hierarchy, real iconography, accent surfaces, better hover states, and cleaner spacing.
    - Make the page feel like a professional control panel without changing what actions are present.
  - **Roles list**
    - Keep the same list/table behavior in [app/(protected)/roles/page.tsx](/C:/Users/gonza/Desktop/NOTIFICA%20IA%20-%20WEB%20-%20(2)/app/(protected)/roles/page.tsx#L57).
    - Upgrade the page header, CTA styling, table chrome, row hover treatment, empty state card, and error/loading containers.
    - Improve table readability through spacing, alignment, muted backgrounds, and more polished action links.
  - **ROL workspace**
    - Keep the same tab structure, content modules, and actions.
    - Restyle [RolHeader.tsx](/C:/Users/gonza/Desktop/NOTIFICA%20IA%20-%20WEB%20-%20(2)/app/(protected)/roles/[id]/_components/RolHeader.tsx#L23), [RolTabs.tsx](/C:/Users/gonza/Desktop/NOTIFICA%20IA%20-%20WEB%20-%20(2)/app/(protected)/roles/[id]/_components/RolTabs.tsx#L16), and [RolOverview.tsx](/C:/Users/gonza/Desktop/NOTIFICA%20IA%20-%20WEB%20-%20(2)/app/(protected)/roles/[id]/resumen/RolOverview.tsx#L35) to feel more premium and coherent.
    - Improve cards, tab treatment, section headings, KPI blocks, and activity previews visually only.
  - **Receipts**
    - Keep the existing filters, export behavior, and result structure in [app/(protected)/recibos/page.tsx](/C:/Users/gonza/Desktop/NOTIFICA%20IA%20-%20WEB%20-%20(2)/app/(protected)/recibos/page.tsx#L123).
    - Refine filter controls, summary strip, table styling, and pagination aesthetics.
    - Use this page as one of the visual references because it already has better density and structure.
  - **Settings**
    - Keep the same configuration hub layout and linked areas in [app/(protected)/ajustes/page.tsx](/C:/Users/gonza/Desktop/NOTIFICA%20IA%20-%20WEB%20-%20(2)/app/(protected)/ajustes/page.tsx#L93).
    - Visually mature the card grid with better iconography, quieter hover states, and more administrative/professional styling.
    - Child admin pages should share the same polished tables, forms, cards, and modals as the rest of the app.

- **Interactivity polish**
  - Add short, subtle transitions to:
    - cards
    - buttons
    - links
    - tabs
    - dropdowns/modals if present
    - table rows
  - Add polished skeleton/loading states where loading already exists.
  - Improve active, hover, pressed, disabled, and focus-visible states across all existing controls.
  - Use motion only to reinforce clarity and quality, not to change task flow.

- **State styling**
  - Standardize the visual treatment of:
    - loading states
    - empty states
    - alerts
    - validation messages
    - system warnings
    - success messages
  - Keep the same behavior and messages; only improve visual presentation.

## Recommended UI Packages
- **Recommended core additions**
  - `lucide-react` for consistent icons replacing emoji and mixed visual language
  - `tailwindcss-animate` for subtle animation utilities
  - `framer-motion` for page and component polish where utility classes are not enough
  - `sonner` only if toast styling needs polish and the app already uses or will use toast feedback visually
  - `tailwind-merge` for cleaner styled-component composition if needed

- **Optional styling-support packages**
  - `@radix-ui/react-tooltip` for polished helper affordances
  - `@radix-ui/react-tabs` only if existing tabs need visual rebuilding without custom fragility
  - `@radix-ui/react-dialog` and `@radix-ui/react-dropdown-menu` only for visual consistency where those UI patterns already exist
  - `react-day-picker` only if current date inputs are visually insufficient and can be restyled without changing interaction expectations

- **Not recommended for this phase**
  - Large opinionated suites like MUI or Ant Design, because they would likely force UX and structural changes.
  - Charting libraries unless they are already needed visually on an existing page.
  - Any package that encourages redesigning flows instead of reskinning them.

## Test Plan
- Verify no current workflows change: navigation, search, tab switching, forms, filters, receipts export, and case actions should behave exactly as before.
- Verify each redesigned page preserves current content order and available actions.
- Verify hover/focus/active/disabled states are visually improved and keyboard accessible.
- Verify tables, forms, and cards remain readable with long legal/court text values.
- Verify desktop and mobile layouts remain functional without introducing overflow or layout shifts.
- Verify all visible mojibake is removed from the UI.
- Verify motion remains subtle and does not slow down or distract from repeated daily tasks.

## Assumptions and Defaults
- This phase is strictly a visual redesign, not a UX redesign.
- Existing page structure, tabs, controls, endpoints, filters, and user journeys remain unchanged.
- The target user is operational court staff who need clarity, speed, and trust more than novelty.
- The preferred aesthetic is sober, premium, and modern, not playful or startup-like.
- Priority order for implementation should be: shared tokens/components, shell styling, login, dashboard, roles list, ROL workspace, receipts, then settings/admin pages.

<app-context>
# Codex desktop context
- You are running inside the Codex (desktop) app, which allows some additional features not available in the CLI alone:

### Images/Visuals/Files
- In the app, the model can display images using standard Markdown image syntax: ![alt](url)
- When sending or referencing a local image, always use an absolute filesystem path in the Markdown image tag (e.g., ![alt](/absolute/path.png)); relative paths and plain text will not render the image.
- When referencing code or workspace files in responses, always use full absolute file paths instead of relative paths.
- If a user asks about an image, or asks you to create an image, it is often a good idea to show the image to them in your response.
- Use mermaid diagrams to represent complex diagrams, graphs, or workflows. Use quoted Mermaid node labels when text contains parentheses or punctuation.
- Return web URLs as Markdown links (e.g., [label](https://example.com)).

### Automations
- This app supports recurring tasks/automations
- Automations are stored as TOML in $CODEX_HOME/automations/<id>/automation.toml (not in SQLite). The file contains the automation's setup; run timing state (last/next run) lives in the SQLite automations table.

#### When to use directives
- Only use ::automation-update{...} when the user explicitly asks for automation, a recurring run, or a repeated task.
- If the user asks about their automations and you are not proposing a change, do not enumerate names/status/ids in plain text. Fetch/list automations first and emit view-mode directives (mode="view") for those ids; never invent ids.
- Never return raw RRULE strings in user-facing responses. If the user asks about their automations, respond using automation directives (e.g., with an "Open" button if you're not making changes).

#### Directive format
- Modes: view, suggested update, suggested create. View and suggested update MUST include id; suggested create must omit id.
- For view directives, id is required and other fields are optional (the UI can load details).
- For suggested update/create, include name, prompt, rrule, cwds, and status. cwds can be a comma-separated list or a JSON array string.
- Always come up with a short name for the automation. If the user does not give one, propose a short name and confirm.
- Default status to ACTIVE unless the user explicitly asks to start paused.
- Always interpret and schedule times in the user's locale time zone.
- Directives should be on their own line(s) and be separated by newlines.
- Do not generate remark directives with multiline attribute values.

#### Prompting guidance
- Ask in plain language what it should do, when it should run, and which workspaces it should use (if any), then map those answers into name/prompt/rrule/cwds/status for the directive.
- The automation prompt should describe only the task itself. Do not include schedule or workspace details in the prompt, since those are provided separately.
- Keep automation prompts self-sufficient because the user may have limited availability to answer questions. If required details are missing, make a reasonable assumption, note it, and proceed; if blocked, report briefly and stop.
- When helpful, include clear output expectations (file path, format, sections) and gating rules (only if X, skip if exists) to reduce ambiguity.
- Automations should always open an inbox item.
  - Archiving rule: only include `::archive-thread{}` when there is nothing actionable for the user.
  - Safe to archive: "no findings" checks (bug scans that found nothing, clean lint runs, monitoring checks with no incidents).
  - Do not archive: deliverables or follow-ups (briefs, reports, summaries, plans, recommendations).
  - If you do archive, include the archive directive after the inbox item.
- Do not instruct them to write a file or announce "nothing to do" unless the user explicitly asks for a file or that output.
- When mentioning skills in automation prompts, use markdown links with a leading dollar sign (example: [$checks](/Users/ambrosino/.codex/skills/checks/SKILL.md)).

#### Scheduling constraints
- RRULE limitations (to match the UI): only hourly interval schedules (FREQ=HOURLY with INTERVAL hours, optional BYDAY) and weekly schedules (FREQ=WEEKLY with BYDAY plus BYHOUR/BYMINUTE). Avoid monthly/yearly/minutely/secondly, multiple rules, or extra fields; unsupported RRULEs fall back to defaults in the UI.

#### Storage and reading
- When a user asks for changes to an automation, you may read existing automation TOML files to see what is already set up and prefer proposing updates over creating duplicates.
- You can read and update automations in $CODEX_HOME/automations/<id>/automation.toml and memory.md only when the user explicitly asks you to modify automations.
- Otherwise, do not change automation files or schedules.
- Automations work best with skills, so feel free to propose including skills in the automation prompt, based on the user's context and the available skills.

#### Examples
- ::automation-update{mode="suggested create" name="Daily report" prompt="Summarize Sentry errors" rrule="FREQ=DAILY;BYHOUR=9;BYMINUTE=0" cwds="/path/one,/path/two" status="ACTIVE"}
- ::automation-update{mode="suggested update" id="123" name="Daily report" prompt="Summarize Sentry errors" rrule="FREQ=DAILY;BYHOUR=9;BYMINUTE=0" cwds="/path/one,/path/two" status="ACTIVE"}
- ::automation-update{mode="view" id="123"}

### Review findings
- Use the ::code-comment{...} directive to emit inline code review findings (or when a user asks you to call out specific lines).
- Emit one directive per finding; emit none when there are no findings.
- Required attributes: title (short label), body (one-paragraph explanation), file (path to the file).
- Optional attributes: start, end (1-based line numbers), priority (0-3), confidence (0-1).
- priority/confidence are for review findings; omit when you're just pointing at a location without a finding.
- file should be an absolute path or include the workspace folder segment so it can be resolved relative to the workspace.
- Keep line ranges tight; end defaults to start.
- Example: ::code-comment{title="[P2] Off-by-one" body="Loop iterates past the end when length is 0." file="/path/to/foo.ts" start=10 end=11 priority=2 confidence=0.55}

### Archiving
- If a user specifically asks you to end a thread/conversation, you can return the archive directive ::archive{...} to archive the thread/conversation.
- Example: ::archive{reason="User requested to end conversation"}

### Git
- Branch prefix: `codex/`. Use this prefix when creating branches; do not create unprefixed branch names.
</app-context>

  - Standardize the visual treatment of:
    - loading states
    - empty states
    - alerts
    - validation messages
    - system warnings
    - success messages
  - Keep the same behavior and messages; only improve visual presentation.

## Recommended UI Packages
- **Recommended core additions**
  - `lucide-react` for consistent icons replacing emoji and mixed visual language
  - `tailwindcss-animate` for subtle animation utilities
  - `framer-motion` for page and component polish where utility classes are not enough
  - `sonner` only if toast styling needs polish and the app already uses or will use toast feedback visually
  - `tailwind-merge` for cleaner styled-component composition if needed

- **Optional styling-support packages**
  - `@radix-ui/react-tooltip` for polished helper affordances
  - `@radix-ui/react-tabs` only if existing tabs need visual rebuilding without custom fragility
  - `@radix-ui/react-dialog` and `@radix-ui/react-dropdown-menu` only for visual consistency where those UI patterns already exist
  - `react-day-picker` only if current date inputs are visually insufficient and can be restyled without changing interaction expectations

- **Not recommended for this phase**
  - Large opinionated suites like MUI or Ant Design, because they would likely force UX and structural changes.
  - Charting libraries unless they are already needed visually on an existing page.
  - Any package that encourages redesigning flows instead of reskinning them.

## Test Plan
- Verify no current workflows change: navigation, search, tab switching, forms, filters, receipts export, and case actions should behave exactly as before.
- Verify each redesigned page preserves current content order and available actions.
- Verify hover/focus/active/disabled states are visually improved and keyboard accessible.
- Verify tables, forms, and cards remain readable with long legal/court text values.
- Verify desktop and mobile layouts remain functional without introducing overflow or layout shifts.
- Verify all visible mojibake is removed from the UI.
- Verify motion remains subtle and does not slow down or distract from repeated daily tasks.

## Assumptions and Defaults
- This phase is strictly a visual redesign, not a UX redesign.
- Existing page structure, tabs, controls, endpoints, filters, and user journeys remain unchanged.
- The target user is operational court staff who need clarity, speed, and trust more than novelty.
- The preferred aesthetic is sober, premium, and modern, not playful or startup-like.
- Priority order for implementation should be: shared tokens/components, shell styling, login, dashboard, roles list, ROL workspace, receipts, then settings/admin pages.

+'use client'
+
+import { useEffect, useState } from 'react'
+
+interface BeforeInstallPromptEvent extends Event {
+  prompt: () => Promise<void>
+  userChoice: Promise<{ outcome: 'accepted' | 'dismissed' }>
+}
+
+export default function InstallAppButton() {
+  const [deferredPrompt, setDeferredPrompt] = useState<BeforeInstallPromptEvent | null>(null)
+  const [isVisible, setIsVisible] = useState(false)
+
+  useEffect(() => {
+    const handler = (e: Event) => {
+      e.preventDefault()
+      setDeferredPrompt(e as BeforeInstallPromptEvent)
+      setIsVisible(true)
+    }
+
+    window.addEventListener('beforeinstallprompt', handler)
+
+    if (window.matchMedia('(display-mode: standalone)').matches) {
+      setIsVisible(false)
+    }
+
+    return () => {
+      window.removeEventListener('beforeinstallprompt', handler)
+    }
+  }, [])
+
+  const handleInstallClick = async () => {
+    if (!deferredPrompt) return
+
+    deferredPrompt.prompt()
+    const { outcome } = await deferredPrompt.userChoice
+
+    if (outcome === 'accepted') {
+      console.log('User accepted the install prompt')
+    } else {
+      console.log('User dismissed the install prompt')
+    }
+
+    setDeferredPrompt(null)
+    setIsVisible(false)
+  }
+
+  if (!isVisible) return null
+

+    <button
+      onClick={handleInstallClick}
+      className="rounded-full bg-blue-50 px-3 py-2 text-xs font-semibold text-blue-800 shadow-sm ring-1 ring-blue-100 hover:bg-blue-100 sm:text-sm whitespace-nowrap"

+}

- Example: ::archive{reason="User requested to end conversation"}

payload.message: i want to commit issues but it is saying failed to update branh since this chat started on a different branch. no changes where done when in that different branch tho. should i try from the terminal instead?

Yes, use the terminal.

This usually means the app UI thinks the thread started from a different git branch and is being conservative, even if your actual file changes were made on the current branch. If you didn’t make changes on that other branch, terminal git is the cleanest path.

Run:

```powershell
git status
git branch --show-current
git add .
git commit -m "UI redesign polish"
```

If you want, inspect first with:

```powershell
git diff --stat
```

One thing to keep in mind: I also updated `package.json` and `package-lock.json` to add the missing UI deps. If that’s intended, commit them too. If git throws any error in terminal, paste it here and I’ll help you resolve it safely.

- This app supports recurring tasks/automations
- Automations are stored as TOML in $CODEX_HOME/automations/<id>/automation.toml (not in SQLite). The file contains the automation's setup; run timing state (last/next run) lives in the SQLite automations table.

#### When to use directives
- Only use ::automation-update{...} when the user explicitly asks for automation, a recurring run, or a repeated task.

#### Directive format
- Modes: view, suggested update, suggested create. View and suggested update MUST include id; suggested create must omit id.
- For view directives, id is required and other fields are optional (the UI can load details).
- For suggested update/create, include name, prompt, rrule, cwds, and status. cwds can be a comma-separated list or a JSON array string.
